messages.subject: Plotting models
parts:
Hello again, 

I was wondering about choise of model. I read that for transect line distance sampling the keys/models: half-normal key with cosine adjustments; half-normal key with Hermite polynomial adjustments; hazard-rate key with simple polynomial adjustments are recommended to be utilised when plotting models. 

My question is if i have to plot first every model without adjustment and then adding the adjustment. Or do i right away plot with the adjustments?

A follow up question to this is if there is a piece of code or function that does this all at the same time and i don't have to plot every possible model?

With kind regards, 

Casolyn van der Schoot

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Plotting models
parts:
Casolyn

Determining the appropriate number of adjustment terms for a given key function model is a matter of model selection. This is done in the Distance R package using the function ds()​. It potentially fits a series of adjustment terms to a specified key function model and uses AIC to determine the appropriate number of adjustments for the data.

You may benefit from reading our online workshop materials that discusses all facets of distance sampling:

https://workshops.distancesampling.org/online-course/
Distance sampling online course
Teaching distance sampling through video lectures and computer exercises.
workshops.distancesampling.org
particularly Chapter 7 for analysing data using R.
